from: June book, night 12 (To Obey Is Best)
p1: The Lord gave King Saul a job and told him how to do it. But Saul did not obey all the way. He kept the best sheep and the big, strong cows called oxen.
Then Samuel came. Saul said, “I have done what the Lord said!”
But Samuel heard sheep saying, “Baa!” and oxen saying, “Moo!” Samuel asked, “What is this sound I hear?”
p2: Saul said the animals were for a sacrifice, a gift to the Lord. Samuel said, “To obey is better than sacrifice.” The Lord wants listening hearts more than any gift. Saul said, “I was afraid of the people.”
Your best gift to Heavenly Father is listening and obeying. Tonight, tell Him one way you will obey, even when others do not.
old: Heavenly Father told King Saul through Samuel: “Fight the Amalekites and destroy everything.” This was a test to see if Saul would obey completely.
Saul fought the battle. But he didn’t obey all the way! He kept the best animals and treasures. He thought, “I’ll sacrifice these to God. That will make up for not obeying.”
Samuel came and heard the animals. “What’s this noise?” he asked. Saul said, “I kept them to sacrifice to God!” Samuel said something important: “To OBEY is better than sacrifice!”
Saul tried to make excuses. But Heavenly Father doesn’t want excuses — He wants obedience! Because Saul disobeyed again, God chose a new king. Obedience matters more than anything!
